(২য় পাতা) তপছিল সম্পত্তি ১। ষ্টেশন লালবাগ ও সাব রেজিষ্ট্রার সদরের অধীন মহল্লা ঢাকেশ্বরী প্রকাশ পুরকতাস্থিত জিলা-ঢাকা কালেক্টরীর তৌজি = ৫২১৭ বিঃ ১নং নিযুক্ত লাখেরাজ তালুক গাঙ্গাঁদেভ্যা অন্তর্গত ঢাকেশ্বরী বাড়ী দক্ষিণ দিক হইতে উক্ত বাড়ী মুখে প্রবেশের রাস্তার ও সেটেলমেন্টের-৪২/৪৩ দাগে ও ৩০ দাগের ঢাকেশ্বরী মন্দির ও ভূমির লাগ পূর্ব সদর দেউরির গর্ভে থানার লাগ পূর্ব দিগেস্থ অতিথী খানা নামক পাকা দালানের ও ৩৫ দাগের জমি ও ঢাকেশ্বরী মন্দিরের দাকিস্থ নাচ মন্দিরের দক্ষিনে চন্ডি দালানের লাগ গভর্ণমেন্টের একোয়ারী ৫৪ দাগের জমির নাল জমির পুরানা সম্পত্তি সম্পত্তি করে পুস্করুনী ৭৯ দাগের পশ্চিম দিগন্ত একোয়ারা গভর্ণমেন্টের ৪৪ দাগের ভূমির সম্পত্তি ন্যাইকের পাশে পশ্চিম জমির সিমানা সারকের অর্থাৎ সেটেল মেন্টের ২৬ দাগের ভূমির পাশে উত্তর এই চৌহদ্দির মধ্যে সেটেলমেন্টে জরিপ সহর ঢাকা সিট নাম্বার ২০ ওয়ার্ড নম্বর ৪.৬.৭.৩ দাগ নম্বর ৩০,৩৭,৩৮,৩৯,৪০.৪১ দাগের ভুমিময় পাকাবাড়ী বিটা মধ্যে জমি অনুমান ৯. বিঘা মুল্য ২০০০০, টাকা ২ ষ্টেশন সাবষ্টেরীর মহল্যা ৩ উক্ত তৌজির অর্থাৎ উক্ত তালুক-স্থিত ঢাকেশ্বরী বাড়ীর পশ্চিম পুস্কারনীর উত্তর অংশের ও উত্তর পারের দক্ষিন অংশের নাগস্পৃষ্ঠ-৪৩ দাগ প্রতাপ চক্রবতির বাগানের লাগ দক্ষিন ঢাকেশ্বরী বাড়ীর পশ্চিম দিগস্থ শীবের মঠ-সকলের লাগ উত্তর ১নং বিবাদীর সত্য দখলীয় ১নং তপছিলের সেটেলমেন্টের ৩০ দাগের জমির উত্তর অংশের লাগ পশ্চিম এই চৌহদ্দীর মধ্যে সেটেলমেন্টে জরিপী ওয়ার্ড সিট ১নং তপছীলের লিখিতানুগ। দাগ নম্বর ৪২ জমি বিখরু কাতা অনুমান ১ বিঘা নিলামী মূল্য-২৫০০ টাকা-……………”

45. The aforesaid schedule shows that the property appertaining to plots No. 41 and 30 were purchased by one Gokul Chandra Roy through auction conducted under Order XXI, rule 94 of the Code of Civil Procedure in an execution proceding under the mentioned rent suit being Civil Decree Suit No. 75 of 1929. 

46. Although, Mr. Siddique assails this fact drawing our attention to the CS Khatian showing that the property was settled without rent and, as such, question of rent suit does not arise. But these are the Certified Copies of the Court Proceedings showing auction purchase, which definitely require to be disapproved by proper adjudication. 

47. The aforesaid claim of respondents showing Gokul Chandra Roy as auction purchaser (owner) of the schedule property gets more strength when Mr. Garib-e-Newaz, learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the Certified Copy of the relevant LA Case No. 2 of 1952-53 where the relevant order sheets as referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondents show that the schedule property was acquired from said Gokul Chandra Roy. Relevant portions of the order sheets arc follows:—
"Land on behalf of M/s Momin Motor & Co, for the establishment of a workshop in Ward No. VI of Dacca Town. 
Order sheet. 
(Rule i29 of the Records manual, 1917).

F& Revenue deptt, with request to stay delivery of possession of the land in question to Momin Motor works Ltd. & further requests to submit a report as to whether the land in question belongs to the Dhakeswari Temple authority or there is any objection on religious ground to the requisition acquisition of the land for the establishment of the Momin Motor works.  Stay further proceeding until further order from Govt. My report in this connection is being submitted to LAC as asked for. 
17-4-52

Is directed by Govt, & LAC a local enquiry into the matter will be held on 20-4-52 at 9.a.m issue notice upon all the interested parties & put up S.R. to me on 19-4-52 positively. 
1-7-52

Anwar Hussain will take necessary action in  the matter immediately & report & send copy of Govt. letter to the R/B to hand over vacant pessn, of there regd. area on or before 14-7-52 put up on 14-7-52. put up on 14-7-52.

None appears to press for the objection petition although the petitioner was asked for to do so fixing to-day as the date of hearing. 
However, I have examined the contents of the objection petition carefully. It appears that  objections have been raised amongst others on the  around that the site being contiguous to the  famous Dhakeswari Temples, the establishment of Motor Workshop there would disturb the peace of the temple and wound the religious sentiment of the Hindu Public. Almost similar objection petitions were submitted by the Same petitioner to DM and to Govt. immediately after the site was brought under requisition. The grounds of objections were thoroughly enquired into and after due consideration of all facts these were rejected by both DM and Govt. In the circumstance stated above the present petition does not appear to me worthy to be tenable. Requisition and acquisition of the site in question  is, therefore, recommended.  
16-1-53 
Seen the petition of the Momin Motor Co. intimating that the wall in the derequisitionedarea is now under the full supervision of the owners of the land who has no objection for the non-removal of the wall in question. Ask the owner Babu Gakul Chandra Roy of Fareashganj to apper on 3.2.53.

FIB Dept. requsting to submit a report the petition dt. 9-4-53 filed by B/Gokul Chandra Roy to the Collector on the points raised there in Acknow ledge receipt of the case record & ask for 10 copies of printed notice of aeqn. when published @ a say that the report on the petn. praying for arbitration is being sent." 
 
48. From the aforesaid order sheets of the relevant LA Case No. 2 of 1952.53, it appears that in the proposed acquired land ownership of the petitioner Deity had not been reflected in an enquiry and rather Gokul Chandra Roy was found the owner of the schedule property. However, in view of submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and the documents as referred to by the contending parties, in particular, the sale certificate issued in the rent execution proceeding by which the schedule property was sold in auction to Gokul Chandra Roy in 1933 and also the order sheets of the relevant LA Case No. 02 of 1952-53 it is reflected that the schedule property was acquired from the auction purchaser Gokul Chandra Roy as the owner of the same. Further, from the order sheet it appears that at the time of acquisition, there was an enquiry considering the fact of existence of a Temple adjacent to the schedule property and it was never raised that the schedule property belonged to the Deity. 

49. Inspite of above scenerio, since by referring to the CS Khatians learned Advocate for the petitioners claims title of the Deity in the acquired property, we are of the view that the writ petition involves a disputed question of facts to be ascertained as to whether before acquisition, the property belonged to the Deity and used for religious worship. Unless it is settled, we are not inclined to adjudicate the legal issue under this Rule Nisi as to the propriety of acquisition made by the respondent-Government under LA case No. 2 of 1952-53 in accordance with sections 3 and 5 of the Act, 1948. In the circumstances, before challenging the acquisition, the petitioners need to institute a properly framed suit before the competent civil Court of jurisdiction to establish the fact that before acquisition the petitioner Deity had title and possession in the schedule property and that the same was used by the public for the purpose of religious worship. 

50. In view of above discussions, we hold that the acquisition made in the year 1952 was for public purpose. However, the 2nd proviso to sections 3 and 5 of the Act, 1948 created an embargo to acquire a property used by the public for religious worship. Unless the schedule property belonged to the Deity, applicability of 2nd proviso to section 3 of the Act, 1948 did not arise. Hence, the petitioner Deity has to establish the facts first through a properly framed suit, that the Deity was owner of the schedule property before the acquisition in question and that the property was used by the public for religious worship at the relevant time of acquisition. 

51. With the above observations, the Rule Nisi is disposed of. The order of status-quo passed at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated. 

Communicate a copy of this judgment and order to the respondents at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub, J: This Civil Appeal by Leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 22.02.2024 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.15376 of 2023 making the Rule absolute. 2. The facts, leading to filing this Civil Appeal, in brief, are as follows: The land in question measuring an area of 8(eight) katha, 11(eleven) chatak of Holding No.10, Block-J, Pragati Sharani Road, Baridhara R/A, Dhaka was allotted by Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (in short, RAJUK) to one Mrs. Anwara Hossain, wife of late Khandakar Mohammad Hossain, on execution of a registered lease deed bearing No.9564 dated 08.07.2002 along with possession thereof. The original allottee subsequently transferred the said property with possession in favour of her daughter, the respondent writ petitioner, vide a deed of Heba dated 20.08.2002 supported by an affidavit. RAJUK having approved the said transfer mutation case was duly opened in her name. Since then she has been enjoying possession of the case property without any objection from any quarter whatsoever. 3. Later, with a view to make a 14(fourteen) storied building, the respondent-writ petitioner entered into an agreement with a developer company on 25.05.2017. In due course of time RAJUK also, gave approval on 22.03.2022 for the construction of building. 4. At this juncture, a banner was erected by the authority concerned indicating that the property in question had been selected for the construction of MRT Line-1 including Entry/Exit Point at the said plot. In the given context, the respondent writ petitioner made an application to the Project Director concerned on 24.09.2023 with a prayer for reconsideration of the location of S08-Natun Bazar Station, DMTCL, MRT Line-1 or in the alternative to redesign in a manner which would minimize the total land acquisition, and thereby ensuring optimal utilization of the land proposed to be acquired, but there was no response. On 09.10.2023, the respondent writ petitioner filed another application to the Project Director concerned with similar prayer. 5. While awaiting the decision thereupon, a notice under Section 4(1) of the “স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণ ও হুকুম দখল আইন, ২০১৭” (in short, the Act, 2017) was issued by the writ respondent no.4 on 29.10.2023 upon the last recorded tenants (as per Dhaka City Survey) notifying all concerned about the proposed acquisition of the land in question for public purpose and public interest, fixing 06.11.2023 for joint survey. In the said notice, persons concerned having interest were also directed to remain present with all relevant documents during the course of joint survey; to that effect, they were requested to apply accordingly. The respondent writ petitioner, however, raised objection thereto on 12.11.2023 under Section 5(1) of the Act, 2017. The Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, writ respondent no.3, upon hearing the respondent writ petitioner, along with others, disposed of the objection on 10.01.2024. 6. Pending disposal of the said objection by the authority concerned meanwhile, the respondent writ petitioner filed Writ Petition No.15376 of 2023 before the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution challenging the impugned show cause notice issued by the writ respondent no.4 under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 vide Memo dated 29.10.2023, to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect. At the same time, the writ petitioner sought for a direction upon the writ respondents, in the form of mandamus, to relocate or redesign the entry-exit, fire exit, ventilation duct point of Natun Bazar Metro Rail Station DMTCL, MRT Line-1 at the land in question. In this regard, the categorical contention of the writ petitioner was that she being the absolute owner of the property in question under RAJUK as such, without serving notice upon her as well as RAJUK, serving notice under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 upon the Dhaka City recorded tenant was without lawful authority. Further assertion of the respondent writ petitioner was that the project is being financed by Japan International Cooperation Agency (in short, JICA) covering 75% of the total cost as loan and that as per the JICA’s Guidelines for Environmental and Social Considerations, 2010 land acquisition and resettlement having impact on affected individuals should be avoided or minimized through alternative design options. In the light of the said guidelines, she made several representations to the authority concerned to reconsider the location of 508-Natun Bazar Station, DMTCL, MRT Line-1, but there was no response. 7. Having found prima facie substance, the High Court Division issued a Rule Nisi vide order dated 04.12.2023 along with interim direction upon the writ respondent no.4 to dispose of the objection of the writ petitioner filed under Section 5(1) of the Act, 2017 within a prescribed period. 8. Challenging the interim direction of the High Court Division dated 04.12.2023, the writ respondent no.1 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.80 of 2024 before this Division. The learned Judge-in-Chamber upon hearing the parties vide order dated 14.01.2024 ultimately, directed the High Court Division to dispose of the Rule Nisi within a prescribed period. 9. The writ respondent no.5, the appellant in the instant Civil Appeal, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that Dhaka City is the capital of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The Dhaka Metropolitan Area has a population of 22.40 million in 2022. Currently, urban transportation in the Dhaka Metropolitan Area relies mostly on road transport, where car, bus, auto-rickshaw, rickshaw, etc. coexist. This creates serious traffic congestion in addition to health hazards being caused by traffic pollution including air pollution. With the rapid national economic growth, the urban population is expected to increase and so will the number of privately owned automobiles. Therefore, improving the urban (public) transportation system in the Dhaka Metropolitan Area, to ease traffic congestion and arrest environmental deterioration, have become a critical issue. 10. Considering the pressing situation, the Government of Bangladesh formulated the “Strategic Transport Plan for Dhaka (STP)” in 2005 in cooperation with World Bank. However, JICA conducted Dhaka Urban Transportation Network Development Study Phase-1 from March, 2009 with the Dhaka Transportation Coordination Authority as its counterpart agency, with the objectives to conceptualize the basic urban development scenario for the Dhaka Metropolitan Area by 2025, and to select priority projects that would help build such a scenario. That study recommended the MRT Line-6 as a priority project. As a result, JICA conducted the feasibility study on MRT Line-6 under Dhaka Urban Transportation Network Development Study Phase-2. Following these studies, the Government of Bangladesh and JICA concluded the loan agreement on the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project in February, 2013 to construct MRT Line-6. Meanwhile, World Bank finished the feasibility study and basic design of Bus Rapid Transit Line 3. On the other hand, Asian Development Bank already completed the basic design of the Bus Rapid Transit Line 3 extension project (from the airport to Gazipur). Under these circumstances, the Government of Bangladesh and JICA made several preliminary discussions upon conducting detailed research on the feasibility of the design in order to identify priority projects in the field of transport sector and accordingly, had agreed to make preparation for Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line 1 and Line 5). 11. However, according to the Final Report of “The Project on the Revision and Updating of the Strategic Plan for Dhaka” (2016 Nov.), Dhaka’s MRT Line-1 originates from Gazipur region and passes through Tongi, then the International Airport; when it reaches Kuril, it divides into a southern branch and an eastern branch. The southern line is aimed to go further to the “Jhilmil Project”, while the eastern line aims to serve the Purbachal development area. The total length of Line-1 is 52 km. and is expected to have the highest passenger demand estimated at 1.9 million per day by 2035 among the sever corridors. 12. Since land acquisition is one of the critical issues for effective implementation of the project concerned several opinions were placed before the authority concerned of Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority in order to minimise land acquisition for maintaining alignment of the MRT line. Moreover, considering the fact that there is an elevated highway between Malibagh and Rampura Stations, it was quite hard to accommodate an elevated MRT structure. In the given scenario, the Project Evaluation Committee proposed for underground option. Accordingly, the said Committee held a meeting on 14.07.2019 on Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line-1). Following the recommendation of the Project Evaluation Committee, cost of the project was fixed at Tk.52,561.4342 crore, out of which Government of Bangladesh is to bear Tk.13,111.1142 crore, while JICA is to provide Tk.39,450.32 crore as loan. In the said meeting estimated time for implementation of the project was fixed from 01.09.2019 to 31.12.2026. The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Roads and Highways Division, Foreign Assistant Branch vide office letter dated 16.08.2018 approved the MRT Line-1 project. Subsequently, Planning Division, NEC-ECNEC issued approval letter of the project on 05.11.2019 to the Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges. The writ respondent no.2 vide office letter dated 20.11.2019 gave administrative approval of the project. Finally, the Roads and Highways Division vide letter dated 26.04.2022 amended the project. Team leader of the Consultancy Firm vide letter dated 28.08.2022 requested the Project Director of Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line-1) for land acquisition plan for North Badda, Notun Bazar Station, based on the requirement of land for the project. 13. Accordingly, the writ respondent no.5 vide office letter dated 14.09.2022 requested the Secretary, Road Transport and Highways Division for acquisition of 2.307 acres of land. In response thereof, the writ respondent no.2 vide letter dated 17.10.2022 gave approval to acquire 2.307 acres of land under Mouza-Vatara, Joar Sahara. Pursuant to the office letter dated 29.12.2022 issued by the writ respondent no.5, the respondent no.2 vide letter dated 09.02.2023 requested the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to take necessary steps imposing restriction upon the transfer, any types of construction and or plantation whatsoever, towards changing the nature of the said 2.307 acres of land. 14. Moreso, on the prayer of the writ respondent no.5, RAJUK vide letter dated 09.02.2023 and the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide letter dated 14.02.2023 respectively issued no objection certificates regarding acquisition of 2.307 acres of land for construction of the 3(three) underground station of MRT Line. 15. Accordingly, writ respondent no.5 vide letter dated 27.02.2023 forwarded all the required documents regarding the project to the Secretary, Road Transport and Highways Division for taking necessary steps for acquisition. The writ respondent no.2 in its turn vide letter dated 28.03.2023 requested the writ respondent no.1 to take necessary steps regarding acquisition of 2.307 acres of land. The writ respondent no.1 vide letter dated 15.05.2023 requested the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to send proposal to the Ministry of Land for acquisition after verification of the concerned documents such as map, plot etc. Pursuant thereto the Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka vide letter dated 07.06.2023 fixed 11.06.2023 at 9.00 a.m. for verification of the boundary of the proposed land. Ultimately, vide letter dated 20.08.2023 respective report was forwarded on 01.08.2023 to the Ministry of Land. Subsequently, the Ministry of Land vide letter dated 05.09.2023 directed the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to complete the process of acquisition. Accordingly, respective notices under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 were issued by the authority concerned upon the city recorded tenants on 29.09.2023 following all legal formalities, as prescribed by law. 16. In this regard, the categorical assertion of the appellant is that to effectuate the crucial requirements for a prolific design of a Standard Entry/Exit, to reduce the cost and loss of existing public/private property and based on the availability of land at Natun Bazar area, the authority concerned had no other option but to select the land in question. 17. Meanwhile, pursuant to the interim direction given by the High Court Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka upon hearing the writ petitioner disposed of her objection filed under Section 5(1) of the Act, 2017 on 10.01.2024 with the following remarks:

Article 42 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, as embodied in Chapter III of the Constitution, guarantees right to property but subject to restrictions imposed by law. However, said right is extinguished by way of compulsory acquisition, nationalization or requisition under the authority of law. Vide Article 42(2) when a law/statute, promulgated by the Legislature in exercise of power as provided under Article 42(1), provides for compensation, it should either fix the amount of compensation or prescribe the principles on which, and the manner in which the compensation is to be assessed and paid. The said law cannot be called in question in any court of law on the ground that its respective provision for compensation is inadequate. 32. Article 42 of the Constitution is, accordingly, quoted below: “42. (1) Subject to any restrictions imposed by law, every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold, transfer of otherwise dispose of property, and no property shall be compulsorily acquired, nationalized or requisitioned save by authority of law. (2) A law made under clause (1) of this article shall provide for the acquisition, nationalization or requisition with compensation and shall fix the amount of compensation or specify the principles on which, and the manner in which, the compensation is to be assessed and paid; but no such law shall be called in question in any court on the ground that any provision of the law in respect of such compensation is not adequate. 33. The Parliament in view of Article 42(1) of the Constitution promulgated “স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণ ও হুকুম দখল আইন, ২০১৭” (Act No. 21 of 2017) relating to acquisition and requisition of immovable property and to provide for matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto. 34. Under the Act of 2017, the process of acquisition commences with the publication of notice under Section 4(1) by the Deputy Commissioner “জেলা প্রশাসক”, as defined in Section 2(5), in the prescribed form and manners, in connection with the properties proposed to be acquired. Said provision does not entail any condition to serve the notice upon the owner of the property in question. Rather, it is a general notice containing the proposition of the authority concerned to acquire the respective property in public interest with right to remain present along with the requiring body on the date and time so fixed for the preparation of joint survey report. Said report shall be the basis for fixing/change of classification of the property, proposed to be acquired and that is also, subject to appeal under Section 4(7). Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 is quoted below: “৪। স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণের জন্য প্রাথমিক নোটিশ জারি:- (১) জেলা প্রশাসকের নিকট কোনো স্থাবর সম্পত্তি জনপ্রয়োজনে বা জনস্বার্থে আবশ্যক মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হইলে তিনি উক্ত সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণের প্রস্তাব করা হইয়াছে উল্লেখ করিয়া উক্ত সম্পত্তির উপর বা সম্পত্তির নিকটবর্তী সুবিধাজনক স্থানে, নির্ধারিত ফরম ও পদ্ধতিতে, নোটিশ জারি করিবেন।" 35. However, prior to publication of the said notice the Deputy Commissioner is required under Section 4(3)(ka) to prepare an inventory, making video with photograph of the actual position and nature of the property proposed to be acquired along with the buildings situated thereon, and or crops and trees which are standing on the said property. 36. Vide Section 4(3)(kha), subsequent to issuance of notice under Section 4(1), the Deputy Commissioner concerned shall prepare “a joint inventory” “যৌথ তালিকা” in the prescribed manner with the participation of the requiring body as well as the person interested in the property, who are to remain present on the respective date and at the respective time. 37. Section 4(4) provides that while preparing the said joint inventory if found any change of classification in the record of the proposed acquired property, the Deputy Commissioner concerned has to endorse his decision to that effect. At the same time, vide Section 4(5) the Deputy Commissioner shall endorse his findings in the said joint inventory whether any house or structure has been or is being constructed with a view to cause prejudice to the public interest. Section 4(6) stipulates the after preparation of joint inventory under Section 4(3) (kha) it shall be displayed in the notice board of the local head office or at any conspicuous place of the respective project site for public gaze. 38. As per Section 4(7), after initiation of proceeding for acquisition under Section 4(3)(ka) if it is found that any construction of building is or is being made with a view to change the nature/classification of the property, said change of classification shall not be enlisted in the said “যৌথ তালিকা”. For non-inclusion of such change in the inventory list is subject to appeal under Section 4(8) before the Commissioner and his decision is final under Section 4(10). 39. However, after selection of site for implementation of the nationally important project Section 4(12) authorizes the Deputy Commissioner to impose restriction, by passing necessary order, on sell, purchase or construction of building on those properties in question. 40. Sections 5 and 6 are quoted below for cursory glance: “৫। (১) ধারা ৪ এর অধীন নোটিশ জারির ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে স্বার্থসংশ্লিষ্ট কোনো ব্যক্তি অধিগ্রহণের বিরুদ্ধে জেলা প্রশাসকের নিকট আপত্তি দাখিল করিতে পারিবেন। (২) জেলা প্রশাসক, উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন প্রাপ্ত আপত্তি, আপত্তিকারী বা তৎকর্তৃক মনোনীত প্রতিনিধির উপস্থিতিতে, দ্রুত শুনানি করিবেন, এবং উক্ত শুনানি বা প্রয়োজনে পুনরায় অনুসন্ধানের পর, উক্ত আপত্তি সম্বন্ধে তাহার মতামতসহ একটি প্রতিবেদন, সাধারণ ক্ষেত্রে উপ-ধারা (১) এ উল্লিখিত সময়সীমা অতিক্রান্ত হইবার পর ৩০ (ত্রিশ) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে এবং জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রকল্পের ক্ষেত্রে ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে, প্রস্তুত করিবেন। (৩) জেলা প্রশাসক- (ক) স্থাবর সম্পত্তির পরিমাণ ৫০ (পঞ্চাশ) বিঘার (১৬.৫০ একর) ঊর্ধ্বে হইলে তাহার মতামত সংবলিত প্রতিবেদনসহ নথি ভূমি মন্ত্রণালয়ের সিদ্ধান্তের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবেন; এবং (খ) স্থাবর সম্পত্তির পরিমাণ ৫০ (পঞ্চাশ) বিঘার (১৬.৫০ একর) নিম্নে হইলে তাহার মতামত সংবলিত প্রতিবেদনসহ নথি কমিশনারের নিকট সিদ্ধান্তের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবেন: তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন কোনো আপত্তি দাখিল করা না হইলে, জেলা প্রশাসক, সাধারণ ক্ষেত্রে, উক্ত উপ-ধারায় উল্লিখিত সময়ের পরবর্তী ১০ (দশ) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে অথবা কমিশনারের লিখিত অনুমতি সাপেক্ষে ৩০ (ত্রিশ) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে এবং জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রকল্পের ক্ষেত্রে ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে, সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিবেন, এবং এতদ্বিষয়ে জেলা প্রশাসকের সিদ্ধান্ত চূড়ান্ত বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে। ৬। (১) ধারা ৫ এর উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীন জেলা প্রশাসক কর্তৃক প্রেরণকৃত প্রতিবেদন বিবেচনার পর ক্ষেত্রমত,- (ক) সরকার উক্ত প্রতিবেদন দাখিলে অনূর্ধ্ব ৬০ (ষাট) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে, এবং (খ) কমিশনার উক্ত প্রতিবেদন দাখিলের ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে অথবা এতদুদ্দেশ্যে লিখিতভাবে কারণ উল্লেখ করিয়া অনূর্ধ্ব ৩০ (ত্রিশ) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে চূড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিবে। (২) সরকার, কমিশনার বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, জেলা প্রশাসক কর্তৃক, উপ-ধারা (১) অথবা ধারা ৫ এর উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীন, স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণে গৃহীত সিদ্ধান্ত জনপ্রয়োজন বা জনস্বার্থে গৃহীত হইয়াছে বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে।” 42. After taking final decision for acquisition of the respective properties the Deputy Commissioner shall issue a general notice under Section 7(1) and (3), in the prescribed form, for taking over possession of the properties in question. Section 7(1) and (3) are quoted below: "৭। স্বার্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যাক্তিকে নোটিশ প্রদানঃ- (১) সরকার, কমিশনার বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, জেলা প্রশাসক কর্তৃক, ধারা ৫ বা ধারা ৬ এর অধীন কোনো স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহণের সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করা হইলে, জেলা প্রশাসক তদমোতাবেক দখল গ্রহণের অভিপ্রায় ব্যক্ত করিয়া নির্ধারিত পদ্ধতিতে সংশ্লিষ্ট স্থাবর সম্পত্তির উপর বা উহার নিকটবর্তী সুবিধাজনক ও দৃষ্টিগ্রাহ্য স্থানে একটি সাধারণ নোটিশ জারি করিবেন। (২)... (৩) অধিগ্রহণের জন্য প্রস্তাবকৃত স্থাবর সম্পতির দখলকার, যদি থাকে, এবং জ্ঞাত বা বিশ্বাসযোগ্য সকল স্বার্থসংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তির উপর নির্ধারিত ফরমে একই পদ্ধতিতে নোটিশ জারি করিতে হইবে।" 43. Section 7(2) and (4), however, have provided an opportunity to the person interested to appear in person on the date, time and place and to place his respective statements of demand of compensation. Section 7(2) and (4) are quoted below: "৭(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন প্রদত্ত নোটিশে অধিগ্রহণের জন্য প্রস্তাবকৃত স্থাবর সম্পত্তির বিবরণ এবং উক্ত সম্পত্তির স্বার্থসংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যক্তিকে অথবা তাহার মনোনীত প্রতিনিধিকে নোটিশ জারির ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবস অথবা জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রকল্পের ক্ষেত্রে ৭(সাত) কার্যদিবস পর জেলা প্রশাসকের নিকট নোটিশে বর্ণিত সময় এবং স্থানে হাজির হইতে হইবে এবং উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে তাহাদের প্রত্যেকের দাবির পরিমাণ এবং ক্ষতিপূরণে তাহাদের স্বত্ত্বের অংশ উল্লেখ করিতে হইবে মর্মে বর্ণনা থাকিতে হইবে। (৩)…………. (৪) জেলা প্রশাসক নোটিশের মাধ্যমে, নোটিশ জারির ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবস অথবা জাতীয় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ প্রকল্পের ক্ষেত্রে ৭(সাত) কার্যদিবস পর, নোটিশে উল্লিখিত স্থানে সংশ্লিষ্ট স্থাবর সম্পত্তিতে অথবা উহার কোনো অংশে অংশীদার হিসাবে, বা বন্ধকগ্রহীতা হিসাবে অথবা অন্য কোনো উপায়ে কোনো দাবি থাকিলে উক্ত দাবির প্রকার, দাবিদারগণের নাম এবং দাবির ফলে প্রাপ্ত বা প্রাপ্য লভ্যাংশ বর্ণনাসহ যথাসম্ভব বাস্তবভিত্তিক একটি বিবরণী যে কোনো স্বার্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যাক্তিকে নাহিল বা করিবার জন্য নির্দেশ প্রদান করিতে পারিবেন।" 44. Vide Section 8(1), after hearing the parties concerned pursuant to the notice of Section 7, the Deputy Commissioner shall enquire on the valuation of the properties in question so made at the time of issuance of notice under Section 4 and also, on the demand of compensation so made by the parties concerned under Section 7(2) and (4). Accordingly, he shall prepare an award of compensation as he deems sufficient (তাহার বিবেচনায়) and also, basing on the last land record and surveys of the respective mouja. Vide sub-section (2) of Section 8 said award shall be treated as final. 45. Section 9 prescribes the respective contexts which shall be taken into consideration while fixing the amount of compensation for acquisition of the properties in question. In particular, Section 9(1)(ka) provides for taking into consideration the market value (বাজারমূল্য) of the respective property in question on the date of publication of notice under Section 4. However, while determining the market value, the Deputy Commissioner shall take into account the average value, to be calculated in the prescribed manner, of the properties of similar description and with similar advantages in the vicinity during the 12 months preceding the date of publication of the notice under Section 4. 46. From a combined reading of the above provisions of law, it is apparent that the Legislature has intended to create respective platforms for the affected person to make his stand at the initial stage of the proceeding of acquisition by remaining present in person with supporting documents while a joint inventory list is being prepared [Section 4(3)(kha)], which is the foundation for preparation of award. Even, prior to finalization of the acquisition process and taking over possession under Section 7, the Legislature has provided scope to the affected person to raise objection on the acquisition process and that said objection shall be mitigated after further enquiry. Even, during pendency of the process of taking over possession the person interested is provided with opportunity to appear in person again, in order to make demand of compensation in support of documents [Section 7(2) and (4)] and upon making due enquiry thereof [Section 8(1)] the Deputy Commissioner is to prepare the award of compensation. In other words, the Legislature vide the above quoted method of assessment has ensured to provide proper and adequate compensation to the affected person for acquisition of the respective properties for greater public interest. 47. In the instant case, after obtaining administrative approval of the Ministry concerned vide Memo No.35.00.0000.065.14.014.21-449 dated 17.10.2022 for acquisition of 2.307 acres of land for construction of “নন্দা, নতুন বাজার এবং উত্তর বাড্ডা স্টেশনের Exit-Entry, Fire-Exit, Ventilation Duct” under Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Development Project (Line-1) and also, on obtaining “No objection” from RAJUK over those properties in question vide Memo No.25.39.0000.030.36.22-175 dated 09.02.2023 a general notice under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 was issued on 29.10.2023 by the authority concerned in connection with L.A. Case No.03.15.08/2023-2024 about the proposed acquisition of the property in question, fixing 06.11.2023 for joint survey. In the said notice, direction was given upon the owner/or person having interest to remain present on the respective date with option to raise objection within 15(fifteen) days of issuance of the said notice. 48. Pertinent to note that in one breath the respondent writ petitioner filed the respective writ petition before the High Court Division challenging the said notice on the plea that it was not served upon her as being the owner of the property; on the other hand, in response to the said notice she filed objection on 12.11.2023, i.e. within 15 (fifteen) days of issuance of the said notice. In response to her objection, the concerned officer of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka vide Process No.219 dated 26.11.2023 requested the respondent writ petitioner to remain present in the office concerned on 04.12.2023 with all relevant documents. On 04.12.2023, her representative duly appeared and was heard along with the representative of the requiring body. On the same date, i.e. on 04.12.2023 the writ petitioner obtained the Rule Nisi, along with interim direction. 49. The above context negates the stand of the respondent writ petitioner to challenge the notice issued under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 on the plea of the same not being served upon her. However, the High Court Division clearly fell into an error in not considering the said factual position of the case, while declaring the impugned notice under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 unlawful. 50. So far seeking direction upon the appellant writ respondents concerned to relocate or redesign the Entry-Exit, Fire Exit, Ventilation Duct Point at the property in question, it appears from record that prior to issuance of the notice under Section 4(1) of Act, 2017 dated 29.10.2023 the respondent writ petitioner filed representation to the appellant writ respondent no.5 on seeing the banner being erected notifying that the property in question was proposed to be acquired for construction of MRT Line-1. In the said representation she made a prayer to reconsider the location of S08 Natun Bazar Station, DMTCL, MRT Line-1 or in the alternative to redesign in such a manner that would minimize the total acquisition from the property in question. Subsequently, she filed another representation to the appellant writ respondent no.5 on 09.10.2023 with similar prayer. 51. Thus, it goes to show that prior to issuance of the impugned notice under Section 4(1) of the Act, 2017 dated 29.10.2023 the respondent writ petitioner had clear knowledge about the proposed acquisition of the property in question. Ultimately, her objection, filed under Section 5(1) of the Act, 2017 on 12.11.2023, had been disposed of by the writ-respondent no.3 on 10.01.2024 negating the prayer on the ground, as quoted above. Said factual position was duly notified to the High Court Division by the contesting writ respondent no.5 by filing affidavit-in-opposition upon annexing the respective order (Annexure-9). 52. At this juncture, giving direction by the High Court Division upon the appellant writ respondent concerned to “consider slight adjustment to the Entry-Exit, Fire Exit, ventilation duct point of Natun Bazar Metro Rail Station DMTCL, MRT Line-1 so that petitioner’s property is not affected”, prior to giving final decision by the writ respondent no.1 on the findings of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka under Section 5(3) of the Act, 2017, clearly falls through as being premature. 53. Apart from the above, we find it pertinent to note from record that subsequent to order dated 10.01.2024 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, pursuant to the objection being raised by the writ petitioner, she made an application to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 28.02.2024 stating, inter alia:

On the said date the concerned authorities duly heard the respective matters. Subsequently, a 7(seven) members committee was formed on 17.04.2024 to conduct joint survey pursuant to the objection(s) being raised on the proposed acquisition of properties, including the property of the respondent writ petitioner. Said committee, upon inspection of the properties on 22.04.2024 gave respective recommendations under Section 5(2) of the Act, 2017 for change of classification of the properties of the respondent writ petitioner including others. Said recommendations were duly approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 27.06.2024. Pursuant to the said approval of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka dated 27.06.2024 the book of joint survey was duly corrected on 30.06.2024 upon changing the classification of the property in question from “বাড়ী” to “দোকান”. Accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka vide order dated 30.06.2024, signed on 14.07.2024, sent all the required documents along with his recommendations under Section 5(3) of the Act, 2017 to the Ministry concerned for its final approval under Section 6(1)(ka) of the said Act, for, the property involved more than 50 (fifty) bigha. 55. Ultimately, the Ministry of Land gave final approval under Section 6(1) of the Act, 2017 vide order dated 17.09.2024 for acquisition of 2.307 acres of land including the land of the respondent writ petitioner. Meanwhile, notice under Section 7(1) of the Act, 2017 had been issued on 23.09.2024 for taking over possession of the property in question. In addition, the concerned authority also, issued notice upon the respondent writ petitioner on 28.11.2024 under Section 8(3)(ka) of the said Act to receive compensation/award. 56. Considering the above undisputed contexts, this Division categorically finds that with the filing of the application dated 28.02.2024 to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for change of classification of the properties in question the respondent writ petitioner has lost/waived her right to oppose the instant Civil Appeal. 57. Accordingly, this Civil Appeal is allowed, however, without any order as to costs. The judgment and order dated 22.02.2024 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.15376 of 2023 is, hereby, set aside. End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 12-5-2024 passed by the High Court Division in Arbitration Application No. 112 of 2024).
full_judgment:
The petitioner filed this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal against the judgment and order dated 12-5-2024 passed by the High Court Division in Arbitration Application No. 02 of 2024. On 30-5-2024, this Division passed the following order:—
"This is an application for stay filed by the petitioner. We have heard the learned Counsels for both the parties and perused the impugned order of the High Court Division as well as other materials on record. 
Upon hearing, the order of status quo granted earlier by this Division be extended till 1st Session of the Arbitration Tribunal in Singapore in SIAC ARBITRATION No. 016 of 2024 (ARB016/24/ZY) AND SIAC ARBITRATION No. 017 of 2024 (ARB017/ 24/ZY). 
However, this order shall not affect any proceedings of the Arbitration Tribunal in Singapore. 
Let this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal be posted in the list on 29-8-2024 for hearing." 

2. Mr. Mohammad Imtiaz Farooq along with Mr. Margub Kabir, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submit that on 30-7-2024 the Arbitration Tribunal was constituted and the order dated 30-5-2024 passed by this Division was produced before the Tribunal by the parties of the arbitration. The Tribunal interpreted the term '1st Session' as to be referring to the 'preliminary meeting' with the parties as per SIAC Rule 19.3. To this effect, the Tribunal in paragraph 70 of its order stated that—
"There is no definition of "1st Session" in the Order. SIAC Rule 19.3 provides for a "preliminary meeting" which, in the Tribunal's view, is the meaning that should be given to "1st Session". Rule 19.3 states that "fals soon as practicable after the constitution of the Tribunal, the Tribunal shall conduct a preliminary meeting with the parties, in person or by any other means, to discuss the procedures that will be most appropriate and efficient for the case." 

3. The learned Counsels submit next that the 1st Session i.e. preliminary meeting was not scheduled at the time of passing the Tribunal's order and the Tribunal observed that the date of such preliminary meeting could be scheduled in a manner that the Petitioner's interim relief application before the Tribunal would be considered prior to holding of the preliminary meeting. However, as per the Tribunal, if this approach were to be taken, it would be beyond the control of the Tribunal as to whether the Honorable Appellate Division would continue its order or not, in particular in the hearing on 29-8-2024. In light of that, the Tribunal anticipated a risk of no protection on the subjected shares being in place if this Division decides to take out the protection before the Tribunal decides on the Petitioner's interim relief application. Considering such risk, the Tribunal decided to pass Procedural Order No. 2 on 21-8-2024 directing the parties not to transfer petitioner's shares in First Dhaka Elevated Expressway Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as FDEE) until further order of the Tribunal. The learned Counsels argue lastly that this Court passed an order on 30-5-2024 and subsequently the Tribunal on 21-8-2024 passed an order on the same matter. Therefore, according to section 7Ka(6) of the Arbitration Act, 2001, if the Tribunal issues an order regarding the matters under section 7Ka(1) of the Arbitration Act any previous order issued by the Court on the same matter will become fully or partially inoperative. 

4. Heard the learned Counsels for the respective parties and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as other materials on record. 

5. It transpires that vide order dated 30-5-2024 this Division extended the order of status quo granted earlier by this Division on 16-5-2024 till 1st Session of the Arbitration Tribunal in Singapore. Subsequently, the Tribunal was constituted on 30-7-2024 and the petitioner-applicant filed an application for urgent interim relief to the Tribunal for an ad interim order of injunction against the transfer of the petitioner's shares in FDEE. Upon considering the urgency of the application, the Tribunal passed the following order on 21-8-2024-
"95. The Tribunal hereby orders that there shall be no transfer of Claimant's shares in FDEE until further order of this Tribunal." 

6. The moment the Tribunal passed the aforesaid order, section 7Ka (6) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 comes into play. Pertinently, section 7Ka (6) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 is extracted below — 
"৭ক। (১)..
(৬) উপ-ধারা (১) এর অধীন প্রদত্ত কোন আদেশ সংশ্লিষ্ট কোন বিষয়ে ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত কোন সালিসী ট্রাইব্যুনাল কিংবা অন্য কোন প্রতিষ্ঠান বা ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক উক্ত বিষয়ে কোন আদেশ প্রদান করা হইলে, সেই বিষয়ে আদালত বা, ক্ষেত্রমত, হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত আদেশ সম্পূর্ণ কিংবা ক্ষেত্রমত উক্ত আদেশের সংশ্লিষ্ট অংশ বিশেষ অকার্যকর হইবে।"

7. The text above reads in translation thus—
"(6) Where any Arbitration Tribunal or any institution or person empowered in any matters relating to orders passed under sub-section (1) passed any order in such matters, the order passed by the Court or High Court Division as the case may be, in the same matter, shall be entirely or the relevant part thereof, inoperative." 

8. It is manifest from the above that if an Arbitration Tribunal issues an order related to matters under section 7Ka(1), any previous order issued by the Court on the same matter will become fully or partially inoperative as per section 7Ka(6). In the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, this Division passed its order on 30-5-2024 and subsequently on 21-8-2024 the Tribunal passed an order on the same matter i.e. status quo on the transfer of the subjected shares. Therefore, considering that the Tribunal passed the order dated 21-8-2024 on the same subject matter of the order dated 30-5-2024 passed by this Division in the instant Civil Petition, section 7Ka (6) of the Arbitration Act, 2001 comes into effect and the matter being in seisin of the Tribunal, the previous order passed by this Division on 30-5-2024 has become infructuous. 

9. In view of the above factual matrix of the case as well as the provisions of section 7Ka (6) of the Arbitration Act, 2001, we are of the considered view that the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal has become infructuous by reason of supervening development as depicted in the preceding discussions. 

The instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is accordingly disposed of as being infructuous. 

End.

lawyer:
Md. Shahadat Tanveer Amin, Advocate ------ For the Petitioners.

parties:
Fazlu Mia (Md.) and another ------ Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs.
Md. Lal Mia and others ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-9-2008 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 142 of 2000 reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-6-2000 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge (In Charge), Belabo, Narsingdi in Title Suit No. 5 of 1999 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 5 of 1999 against the petitioners as defendant in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Belabo, Narsingdi on the following prayers.

(ক) নালিশা ভূমির বিষয়ে বাদীগণের বরাবরে দলিল রেজিঃ করিয়া দেওয়ার জন্য বাদীগণের অনূকুলে ও বিবাদীগণের প্রতিকুলে এক ডিক্রী দিতে।

(খ) আদালত কর্তৃক নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে বিবাদীগণ বাদীগণ বরাবরে দলিল রেজিঃ করিয়া না দিলে প্রয়োজনীয় রেজিঃ খরচ ও মুসাবিদা দাখিলের নির্দেশ দানে আদালত মাধ্যমে দলিল রেজিঃ করিয়া দেওয়ার এক আদেশ দিতে।

(গ) বাদীগণ বরাবরে নালিশা ভূমির ফরমাল দখল বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার অপর এক আদেশ দিতে।

3. The facts as figured in the plaint, are that, the defendants as owner of the schedule property covered by SA Khatian Nos. 70 and 584, measuring 13 decimals sold the same to the plaintiffs at a consideration of Taka 3,000 and accordingly, the defendants executed a sale deed on 30-10-1997 in favour of the plaintiffs with a promise that they will register the deed later on. The defendants on this and that plea took time and ultimately refused to give registration of the sale deed executed by them. The plaintiffs then, once again requested them and finally served a legal notice upon the defendants on 12-7-1988 demanding registration of the sale deed but the defendants did not come forward to register the sale deed executed by them. Consequently, the plaintiffs finding no way out have constrained to file the present suit praying for a direction upon the defendants to register the deed executed in favour of the plaintiffs.

4. The petitioners as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, briefly stating, that the defendants agreed to sell only 1 decimal of land at a consideration of Taka 3,000 to the plaintiffs but while the plaintiffs preparing the sale deed, in collusion with the scribe, the quantum of land has been written in the schedule to the deed as 13 decimals in place of 1 decimal and took LTI of the defendants on the sale deed. Before taking LTI the sale deed was not read over to the defendants. After putting LTI, on the defendants' insistences the scribe read over the same and thereafter, the defendants came to know that the quantum of land in the deed has been written 13 instead of 1 decimal. Finding this discrepancy in the document the defendants refused to give registration of the same and delivery of possession of the suit land and asked the plaintiffs to correct the deed. But the plaintiffs with malafide intention and to grab the property of these poor defendants did not correct the quantum of land written in the deed for which the defendants refused to give registration of the deed in favour of the plaintiffs.

5. In course of hearing, the plaintiffs examined three PWs. and filed the deed in question in court but the defendants adduced no evidence on their behalf. The trial court upon contested hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 28-6-2000. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 142 of 2000 before the learned District Judge, Narsingdi. Eventually, the said appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narsingdi on transfer who after contested hearing allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment of the trial court by its judgment and decree dated 14-9-2008. At this stage, the defendant-respondent-petitioners moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

6. Mr. Shahadat Tanveer Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the trial court rightly dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs holding that in the suit area selling of 13 decimals land at a consideration of Taka 3,000 only is not at all believable and the plaintiffs failed to prove that in the concerned area at that time the property in question was sold at the rate as shown in the alleged deed of sale. On appeal the appellate court without reversing and adverting the findings and observations of the trial court most unfortunately held that the defendants are to prove that the property in the area at that time was sold at a rate of Taka 3,000 per decimal. He further submits that the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable in law as the definite case of the plaintiffs is that the defendants executed a sale deed in their favour but they refused to give registration of the same in favour of the plaintiffs. In the situation, the proper action for the plaintiffs are to take recourse under sections 72 to 76 of the Registration Act and thereafter to file a suit under section 77 but the plaintiffs without taking any step under the said provisions of law directly approached the court below with a prayer for directing the defendants to give registration of the deed failing which to get registration through court which is beyond the jurisdiction of the trial court and, as such, the suit is barred by section 77 of the Registration Act. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Rahisuddin Fakir vs Naresh Chandra Chakraborti, 8 DLR 648, Md Asiruddin vs Bazlur Rahman, 34 DLR 215 and Md Moshahaq Ali Mia vs Rabeya Khatun, 37 DLR (AD) 190.

7. Mr Md Mizanur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that it is not denied by the defendants that they did not execute the sale deed in question but the only ground they have taken is that the plaintiffs have written quantum of land as 13 decimals instead of 1 decimal in the sale deed. In the situation, as argued, by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, the plaintiffs have no other alternative remedy but to approach the court with a prayer for direction upon the defendants to register the sale deed duly executed by them and, as such, the suit is well maintainable. It is also argued that the civil court has jurisdiction under section 9 of Code of Civil Procedure to try all suits of civil nature. This is a case of civil nature and, as such, the suit is maintainable in law. He further submits that the defendants cannot raise any objection regarding quantum of land after execution of the sale deed and the court is not also under any obligation to scrutiny and to see whether the defendants sold 13 decimals or 1 decimal of land. The only question for the court to decide whether the sale deed was executed by the defendants. If it is proved that the defendants executed the sale deed, the court shall direct the executants to register the same in favour of the plaintiffs. Mr Rahman further submits that the appellate court rightly observed that it was incumbent upon the defendants to prove that the property in the concerned area at the relevant time was sold at a consideration of Taka 3,000 per decimal but the defendants failed to prove the same and on that finding decreed the suit by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and, as such, the appellate court has not committed any error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

8. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, gone through the application, impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below and the evidences both oral and documentary lying in the lower court records.

9. In the present case, admittedly the deed of sale in question was duly executed by the defendants in suit. It is also found that the defendants are illiterate and, as such, they executed the deed in question by putting their LTI that is why it is imperative to consider that the executants had no knowledge about the quantum of land contained therein. The trial court in its judgment observed that in the present marker, selling of 13 decimals land at a consideration of Taka 3,000 only is not at all believable. Moreover, the plaintiffs could not produce any evidence to the effect that at the relevant time in the concerned area the property was sold at the rate shown in the sale deed in question. The appellate court in allowing the appeal shifted the burden of proof upon the defendants simply observing that the defendants did not deny the execution of the sale deed without considering other legal aspect of the proceedings.

10. From perusal of the judgment and decree, it has come to the notice of this Court that both the courts below failed to appreciate the provisions of law contained in sections 72-76 of the Registration Act applicable in the present case. For getting a kabala registered, duly executed by the vendors, the purchasers ought to have made an application by filing the sale deed before the Registering Officer seeking registration of the same with notice to the executants. In the event of refusal by the Registering Officer the purchaser shall file an appeal before the District Registrar and in the event of refusal by the District Registrar the purchaser is to file suit under section 77 of the Registration Act before the civil court. Any document or sale deed executed by any person to be presented before the Registering Officer within 4 months from the date of execution of the same or within the time extended by the Registrar but in the present case the plaintiffs did not present the deed in question before the Registering Officer within the time fixed by law rather they directly filed the suit before the civil court with a prayer for a direction upon the defendants to register the deed in question in favour of the plaintiffs on 8-3-1999 i.e. after one and a half year of the execution of the deed in question by the defendants. The prayer contained in the plaint is a direction upon the defendants to cause registration of the deed and to deliver possession of the land to the plaintiffs. The prayer for direction can only be made in a suit under section 77 of the Registration Act. Prayer for having a deed registered through court and delivery of possession can be made in a suit for specific performance of contract only but the present suit is not as such.

11. Now the question is whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief on the prayers made in the plaint for a direction upon the defendants to give registration of the document. One fatal objection to such a suit is that the document sought to be registered cannot, except under the special provisions of section 77, be received in evidence and therefore, the court cannot ascertain that there is a document requiring registration. Another objection is that by section 23 of the Registration Act, subject to the provisions of sections 24, 25 and 26 no document other than a will shall be accepted for registration unless presented for that purpose within 4 months from the date of execution. Unless, therefore, the decree compelling registration were passed within four months from the date of execution of the document or at least within the additional 4 months to which the registrar may extent the time, the decree of the court would be a nullity. The Registering Officer could not be compelled to do that which the law forbids him to do. Moreover, I think that such a suit will not lie upon the general principle that, when a statute creates a right or an obligation or provides a method for enforcing it, that method and not the remedy at common law must be followed.

12. The appellate court is in an error in supposing that in the present case no action under Registration Act could have been taken by the plaintiffs. It seems to have omitted to notice that documents can be presented for registration only by the executants but also by any person claiming under the document. Plaintiffs therefore, who had possession of the document, within time allowed for registration, could have presented it for registration and obtained summons for defendants' appearance under section 86 of the Registration Act. If defendants had appeared and admitted execution, the document would have been registered. If they had denied execution, registration would have been refused and the plaintiffs would have been entitled to get an enquiry before the registrar under sections 73-76 of the Registration Act. If defendants did not appear, the plaintiffs might have proved execution of the document and on such proof would have been entitled to registration. If the Registering Officer was not satisfied with their evidences of execution and refused to register, an appeal would have lain to the Registrar under section 72. If the decision of the Registrar under sections 72 or 76 had been adverse to the plaintiffs they would have had a remedy by suit under section 77 of the Registration Act. Plaintiffs had therefore, a complete remedy under the Act and not having chosen to follow it have only themselves to blame that the efficacy of the document has not been completed by registration.

13. There remains the question whether plaintiffs can have a decree such as the appellate court has given them. In my opinion the plaintiffs are not entitled to such relief. The court can give relief to any person for Specific Performance of Contract where some acts and deeds remained pending for the party against whom the decree was sought for but in the present case after execution of the sale deed by the defendants they have had nothing remain to perform on their part. It is the duty of the plaintiffs to approach the Registering authority to get the deed in question registered and in the event of refusal by them the remedy lies under section 77 of the Registration Act and in a suit under this provision of law the court can legally direct Registering authority to register the deed in question within the time fixed by the court.

14. From a perusal of the plaint, it appears that the Registering Officer or the authority has not been made party to the suit. The principal-defendants in suit are the persons who executed the sale deed who already performed their part and, as such, decree cannot be passed against the defendants in the absence of Registering Authority. Therefore, no suit shall lie to compel the defendants to do an act which they already done. The only course ought to have been followed by the plaintiffs as provided in sections 73-76 followed by a suit under section 77 of the Registration Act, but they failed to do so.

<u>15. It is to be mentioned that in a case like the present there were two alternative remedies available to the plaintiffs. It was open to them either to bring a suit under section 77 of the Registration Act merely for the registration of the document within thirty days of refusal by the Registrar to register the document. It was equally open to them to have recourse to the fuller and more comprehensive remedy provided by a suit for specific performance of contract of sale. Since the question of validity of the sale deed has been raised in the present case it must be determined in a suit properly framed for that purpose and the scope of that suit is obviously much wider than that of a suit under section 77. The plaintiffs instead of filing a properly framed suit directly approached the trial court praying for a direction upon the executants of sale deed to register the same without impleading Sub-Registrar and Registrar of the concerned district as defendants in suit. Had it been a simple suit for specific performance of contract it would not be barred merely on the ground that the plaintiffs did not choose to bring a suit under section 77 of the Registration Act.</u>

16. In the facts and circumstances stated hereinabove, this Court finds that the appellate court has committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Therefore, this court is inclined to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below.

17. In the result, the rule is made absolute however, there will be no order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 14-9-2008 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narsingdi in Title Appeal No. 142 of 2000 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 20-6-2000 passed by the Senior.

18. Assistant Judge, Belabo, Narsingdi in Title Suit No. 5 of 1999 is hereby restored with the findings and observations made in the body of this judgment.

19. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

20. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.

VS

full_judgment:
Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder, J: On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule, at the instance of the Petitioners was issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the order dated 12-10-2025 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 495 of 2025 refusing the application for early hearing and rescheduling the date, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as this court may deem fit and proper. 

2. The facts of the Petitioners' suit relevant to disposal of the Rule, in nutshell, are that the petitioner No. 1 entered into a share purchase agreement with Opposite Party No. 2 for acquisition of equal number of shares of Opposite Party No. 1 Company, and invested a substantial amount of money to construct and operate a Luxury Boutique Hotel in the Uttara area of the capital city of Dhaka. The said Agreement was partly acted upon by the Opposite Party No. 2 since the agreed numbers of shares were allotted in favour of the Petitioners, share certificates were issued, and the Petitioner No. 2 was inducted in Board by appointing him as the Chairman of the Opposite Party No. 1 Company. Subsequently, certain disputes arose with regard to the non-compliances of some terms and condition of the said Agreement. Upon alleged non-compliance with the terms of the agreement, the Petitioners invoked arbitration for the resolution of the dispute in accordance with the arbitration clause contained therein and sought interim protection amongst other before the Learned District Judge by filling an application under section 7A of the Arbitration Act, 2001 particularly regarding the operation of the Company's bank accounts, and restraining order on transfer of immovable properties prior to the constitution of the arbitral tribunal. The learned District Judge, Dhaka granted interim injunction and thereby put an embargo requiring the signature of the petitioner No. 2, the Chairman of the Company in the operation of the Company's bank account, and further restrained the Opposite Party No. 1 Company from transferring any of its property and shares, by an order dated 01-12-2024, which was extended from time to time, and finally it was extended until the constitution of the arbitral tribunal. Against the said order the Opposite Party No. 2, filed the Civil Revision No. 342 of 2025 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division, by its order dated 26-1-2025, stayed the said interim order passed by the Learned District Judge, but the opposite party was restrained by the High Court Division from transferring any of its property and shares of the Company. In the meantime, the tribunal was constituted, and the petitioners moved an application under section 21 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 seeking an interim order from the Constituted Arbitral Tribunal as the interim order passed by the Learned District Judge expired upon the constitution of the Tribunal, and accordingly the Tribunal passed an interim order directing the joint operation of bank accounts and holding of board meetings, and imposed a restraining order on the transfer of movable and immovable properties. Challenging the said interim order of the Tribunal, the Opposite Parties, moved before the High Court Division, by filing the Arbitration Application No. 10 of 2025 under section 20 of the Arbitration Act 2001, and obtained an order of stay by the order dated 19-5-2025. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order of stay, the Petitioner filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal being No. 2177 of 2025, wherein the Appellate Division passed an order of stay however did not interfere with the interim order passed by the Arbitral Tribunal so far as it relates to the joint operation of Bank Account and injunction on the transfer of properties and shares by its order dated 28-7-2025. When the aforesaid interim restraining orders were in force, the Respondent No. 2, was operating the Bank account of the Company by his sole signature being Account No. 1512101000005059 maintained with the United Commercial Bank PLC, Nikunja Branch, Le Meridien, Finance Square, Commercial Block, Nikunja, Khilkhet, Dhaka, by replacing the name of Hotel as "Emerald Dhaka Luxury Hotel" with effect from 01-9-2025 in the same premises keeping the Petitioners in complete dark. 

3. Upon such factual development, the Petitioners filed an application under section 21(4) of the Arbitration Act 2001 before the District Judge once again for enforcement of the interim order passed by the Arbitral Tribunal which was eventually affirmed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division. The Petitioners in the said application prayed the following reliefs: 
"A) Issue notice upon the Respondent Nos. 1&2 to show cause as to why the interim protective order of the Arbitral Tribunal passed vide Order No. 4 dated 25-3-2025, and subsequently affirmed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division vide Order dated 28-7-2025 passed in the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2177 of 2025 shall not be enforced in accordance with section 21(4) of the Arbitration Act, 2001, and after hearing of the parties and perusing the records and cause shown, if any, be pleased to—
